description: Issue #956: neutralizes JsonFileDashboardService.ValidateWidgetConfigs' write-time header guard by forcing the RestOptions.Headers validation block to never execute via a compile-preserving `false &&` prefix (mirrors the established pattern from 948-dashboard-restoptions-egress-write-guard-neutralize -- not a compile-time constant since the right-hand operand is a runtime property/method result, so no CS0162 unreachable-code warning). This reintroduces the write-time half of #956's defect: a caller can persist a 'rest' widget whose RestOptions.Headers carries too many headers, or headers whose combined name+value length exceeds the cap, with no rejection and no signal to an operator reviewing the definition -- the header-NAME hard-reject case (Host/Transfer-Encoding/etc.) is exercised by the send-time sibling mutant (956-restwidget-header-send-time-guard-neutralize) rather than duplicated here, since both guards call the SAME RestWidgetDataSource.ValidateHeaders implementation and this entry only needs to prove THIS call site is load-bearing. red_tests are the count-cap and size-cap rejections (both non-parameterized MSTest methods, unlike the DataRow-based per-header-name test in the same class -- run_mutant.py's TRX parser keys results by className.methodName only, so a DataRow method's multiple outcomes would silently collapse to whichever data row's UnitTestResult is processed last in the TRX, which is not a reliable gate signal). green_test is the Authorization+custom-header positive control, proving the guard's blast radius is the hard-rejected/count/size checks specifically, not 'rest' widgets with Headers in general.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Dashboard.Dash: Assert\.ThrowsException failed\. Expected exception type:<System\.ArgumentException> but no exception was thrown
Assert\.ThrowsException failed\. Expected exception type:<System\.ArgumentException> but no exception was thrown

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured by applying the patch manually and running exactly as run_mutant.py does (`dotnet build -c Release` then `dotnet test -c Release --no-restore --filter <red_test_filter>`) before writing this file, then reverting the manual patch application and letting run_mutant.py apply/run/revert it itself for the actual gate run. Both declared red tests failed with exactly this message (MSTest's own Assert.ThrowsException -- confirmed identical between Debug and Release). Also ran the full DashboardWidgetConfigValidationTests filter (29 tests, including the 8 hard-rejected-header-name DataRow cases and the AllowPrivateNetwork/AllowHttp/AllowedPorts groups) under the same mutant beforehand: only the two declared tests failed; every other test, including the positive control and the unrelated AllowedPorts/AllowPrivateNetwork guards (separate code paths, untouched by this patch), stayed green.
